faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then multiply by 52. For a standard 38-hour week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, the annual gross is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. faqs.q: What is the casual loading and how does it affect my pay?

For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 + 25%). This loading is included in the rate you see; you should not add it yourself. Learn more on our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page.

faqs.q: How is tax calculated on my annual salary?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates are: 0% on the first $18,200, 15% on income between $18,201 and $45,000, 30% on $45,001–$135,000, 37% on $135,001–$190,000, and 45% above $190,000. bodyMarkdown:
## Introduction

Understanding your pay starts with knowing how an hourly rate translates into an annual salary, a fortnightly amount, and what you take home after tax and super. Whether you are checking an offer or comparing jobs, the formula is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For most full-time roles, the standard is 38 hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This article explains the conversion, the National Minimum Wage, casual loading, tax, and super, and touches on why searching for "jordan bos salary" might not give you the full picture.

## The Formula: Hourly to Annual

To estimate your annual gross salary, use:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

If you work 38 hours per week, the calculation becomes:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, the annual figure is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44. Your fortnightly gross (before tax) is the weekly amount multiplied by 2. A 38-hour week at $26.44 gives $1,004.90 per week, so a fortnight is $2,009.80.

This formula assumes you are paid the same rate every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It is a starting point for budgeting and comparing offers. Use our [the timesheet](/) to enter your base rate and see the annual equivalent.

## National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week, as published by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This is the legal minimum for award-free employees. Most workers are covered by an industry or occupation award, which sets higher minimum rates. For example, the Children’s Services Award and Pharmacy Award have additional increases from gender-based undervaluation reviews. Always check the relevant award using the [pay guides](/blog) on our site.

Award rates vary by classification and experience. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay and Conditions Tool can help you find your exact rate. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 in May 2026, well above the minimum, reflecting the diversity of Australian wages.

## Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (sick leave, annual leave). The casual National Minimum Wage is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 + 25%). This loading is already included in the rate you see on pay guides; never add it yourself. If you are casual, your annual estimate should use the loaded rate. For more details, see our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page.

## Tax and Medicare

Once you have your annual gross, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% on the excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: $51,370 plus 45% on the excess over $190,000

A Medicare levy of 2% generally applies, with reductions for low-income earners (using 2025–26 single thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). Tax is withheld by your employer through PAYG. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a personalised estimate.

## Superannuation

Superannuation is paid on top of your salary. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). For example, on a $52,269 annual salary, super would be $6,272.28 per year, added to your super fund, not to your take-home pay. This is not deducted from your gross; it is an extra cost for your employer. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

## The Jordan Bos Salary Context

You might search for "jordan bos salary" to see what a professional footballer earns. However, individual salaries for athletes are not published by the Fair Work Ombudsman or the Australian Bureau of Statistics. They are determined by private contracts, often well above award rates. The National Minimum Wage and award rates apply to most Australian workers, not high-profile sportspeople. If you are curious about a specific person’s pay, you would need to look at publicly available contract details or media reports. For your own pay, focus on your hourly rate and the award or agreement that covers you.

## Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
